title: The complete wedding planning checklist for every stage
seo_title: The Complete Wedding Planning Checklist: A Step-by-Step Guide
dek: This definitive wedding planning checklist provides a month-by-month timeline to help you organise your budget, find a venue and manage every supplier for an efficient celebration.
body:
According to Bridebook's 2026 UK Wedding Report, the average engagement now lasts 23.8 months. This extended timeline offers a significant advantage: it allows you to spread out the administration and use this wedding planning checklist to secure your first-choice suppliers before their diaries fill up.

## The ultimate wedding planning checklist: 12 months and beyond

The first year of wedding planning involves setting the pillars that support every other decision. This initial stage of your wedding planning checklist focuses on the foundations: budget, guest count and venue. According to Bridebook's 2026 UK Wedding Report, the average wedding cost in the UK is 20,604 pounds. While this is a helpful benchmark, a quarter of couples spend 10,000 pounds or less, and many luxury celebrations exceed 30,000 pounds.

### Establish your wedding budget
Before researching venues or attire, you must determine your total spend. This figure dictates the scale of the event and the type of specialists you can hire. Data from the 2026 report shows that over half of the average budget (51%) is typically allocated to venue hire and catering. Other significant portions include:

* Wedding attire: 19%
* Photography and videography: 10%
* Flowers and décor: 7%
* Entertainment: 5%

If you are working with a modest budget, consider off-peak months such as January, February or October, which are often more affordable than summer dates. Choosing a registry office for the ceremony is another way to reduce costs, as these are often the most affordable legal options in the UK.

### Draft the guest list
Your guest list and venue choice are intrinsically linked. A large guest list requires a high-capacity space, while a micro wedding of fewer than 50 people may feel lost in a grand ballroom. Start with a rough number of people you can afford to accommodate.

The average cost per guest in 2026 is 278 pounds. To manage costs, some couples categorise their list into those they feel are essential to the celebration and those they would like to have present if the budget and capacity allow. Sorting this list early prevents disagreements and ensures you look for venues with the correct capacity.

### Secure your venue and date
Securing a venue is the priority once the budget and guest count are settled. This decision often dictates the wedding date. If you have a specific date in mind for emotional reasons, you may need to be flexible with the location. Conversely, if you have a specific venue in mind, you might need to choose a date based on their availability.

Venues often book up several years in advance, especially for summer weekends. As you begin to research businesses and compare styles, the Roko Directory lists [all event and wedding businesses](/wedding-vendors) to help you identify specialists that align with your vision. Locking in your venue early ensures your first-choice specialists are available before their diaries fill up. If you are planning a civil ceremony, remember that you must give notice of marriage at your local register office at least 28 days before the wedding.

## Legal requirements and notice of marriage

To ensure your marriage is legally valid in England and Wales, you must meet specific criteria: you cannot be closely related to your partner and neither of you can be currently married or in a civil partnership. Same-sex couples are permitted to marry or convert an existing civil partnership into a marriage in these regions.

### Giving notice of marriage
The most significant administrative step in your wedding planning checklist is giving notice. This involves attending an appointment at a local register office to sign a legal statement of your intention to marry. By law, this must be completed at least 28 days before your ceremony.

This notice is specific to your chosen venue. Consequently, you should only book this appointment once your location is confirmed. If you decide to change your venue after giving notice, you will usually need to repeat the process and pay the associated fees again.

### International and regional rules
If you or your partner are from outside the UK or Ireland, the process may involve additional steps. You might need to apply for a marriage visitor visa or another relevant permit before you can give notice or marry in the UK. It is essential to consult official GOV.UK guidance to confirm which documents you require, as these rules depend on your specific residency status and where you currently live.

It is also important to remember that legal procedures vary across the UK. Scotland and Northern Ireland operate under different rules to England and Wales. If you are planning a ceremony abroad, the legal requirements will depend entirely on the destination country. For help managing these logistics, you can find wedding planners on Roko (/wedding-planning) who specialise in coordinating the administrative and practical details of the day.

## Securing your core supplier team

The period between 9 and 12 months before your wedding is often described as the vendor era. This is when you lock in the professionals who will capture and set the tone for the celebration. Because high quality photographers, videographers and musicians often book up a year or more in advance, securing these contracts now ensures you get your first choice rather than settling for who is available. Before booking independent caterers, check if your venue has a list of set suppliers they require you to use, as this may dictate your options.

### Photography and videography
According to Bridebook's 2026 UK Wedding Report, couples continue to prioritise professional documentation. The average spend for photography is £1,484, while videography averages £1,514. When choosing these suppliers, review their full portfolios to ensure their style matches your vision.

If your chosen photographer is not local to your venue, you must account for travel expenses. Ask early whether they require a mileage fee, train fares or overnight accommodation. Adding these costs to your initial budget prevents surprises during the final payment stage. If you are hiring a team from a different region, remember that supplier costs vary: London professionals typically charge 30 percent above the national average, while those in Yorkshire and the Humber often charge 12 percent less.

### Music and entertainment
Entertainment is a significant driver of the guest experience. In 2026, the average cost for reception music is £1,061, with ceremony music averaging £845. Other forms of entertainment, such as magicians or photo booths, typically cost around £844.

| Supplier Type | Average Cost (2026) |
| :--- | :--- |
| Photographer | £1,484 |
| Videographer | £1,514 |
| Reception Music | £1,061 |
| Ceremony Music | £845 |
| Other Entertainment | £844 |

### Managing the logistics with a wedding planning checklist
As your team of suppliers grows, the logistics of coordinating arrival times, dietary requirements and equipment needs become more complex. If the thought of managing multiple contracts and schedules feels heavy, you can find wedding planners on Roko who specialise in handling these details. A professional planner can bridge the gap between your vision and the practicalities of the day, often for an average investment of £1,543.

Using a wedding planning checklist during this 9 to 12 month window allows you to tick off these high priority bookings early. This not only secures your preferred dates but also gives you a clearer picture of your remaining budget for décor, attire and flowers.

## Defining your style and wedding attire

Your venue choice often dictates the aesthetic of the celebration. Once the location is secured, you can begin to define a cohesive theme. Whether you are planning a formal black-tie event in London or a relaxed celebration in a rural barn, your attire and décor should reflect the setting. Bridebook's research suggests that a wedding theme often materialises after you have visited your venue a few times, as the architecture and surroundings influence your choices for flowers and styling.

### Budgeting for fashion

According to Bridebook's 2026 UK Wedding Report, wedding attire typically accounts for 19 per cent of the total budget. On average, couples spend £1,532 on a dress and £859 on menswear, before the cost of accessories is added. Setting these parameters early helps you focus your search on designers and boutiques within your price range. You can browse a wide range of [wedding specialists on Roko](/wedding-vendors) to find boutiques and tailors that match your specific aesthetic.

### The shopping timeline

Start shopping for dresses and suits 9 to 12 months before the wedding. It is a common misconception that you will find the right outfit at your first appointment. Identifying the right look often takes several visits to different boutiques, so giving yourself a three-month window for research prevents unnecessary pressure.

By the 6 to 9 month mark, you should aim to have your wedding dress ordered. This provides sufficient time for the garment to be manufactured and for multiple alteration appointments to be scheduled. This window also allows you to find accessories that complement the look.

| Item | Average Spend (2026) |
| :--- | :--- |
| Wedding dress | £1,532 |
| Menswear | £859 |
| Accessories | £449 |

When visiting boutiques, consider the practicalities of your venue. A heavy satin gown may be uncomfortable for a summer outdoor ceremony, while a lightweight linen suit might not provide enough warmth for a winter celebration. Use these early appointments to test different fabrics and silhouettes against your chosen theme, ensuring the final choice is both stylish and functional for the environment.

## Beauty trials and save the dates

The period between six and nine months before the wedding is when the aesthetic vision begins to crystallise into firm bookings. With the venue and date secured, you can focus on the personal details that define the look and feel of the celebration.

### Ordering your wedding attire
Whether you have selected a gown from a bridal boutique or found an outfit during an online search, now is the time to place your order. Bridebook's planning guidance suggests that ordering at this stage provides enough time for professional alterations and allows you to find accessories that complement the fabric and cut. If you are shopping for suits, this window also allows for bespoke tailoring or the coordination of hire sets for the wedding party.

### Securing hair and makeup artists
With your outfit confirmed, you can secure a hair and makeup artist who understands your style. Roko suggests reviewing social media profiles or asking for recommendations to find a professional whose previous work aligns with your vision. 

A trial is a vital step during this window. Most stylists suggest meeting around six months before the date to test different looks and ensure you are comfortable with their technique. This trial period allows you to see how the products wear over several hours and ensures the stylist can create the specific look you want for the wedding day. It is also an opportunity to discuss your skincare or hair care routine leading up to the event to ensure a healthy base for the application.

### Sending save the dates
To ensure your guests can attend, send your save the dates as soon as the date and venue are locked in. While traditional printed cards remain a popular choice, digital save the dates are increasingly used for their efficiency. According to Bridebook, digital versions are often more cost-effective, allowing you to reallocate funds to other areas of the budget while providing guests with an immediate way to mark their calendars.

### Finalising floral and decor plans
This is also the time for meetings with your florist and decor suppliers. Use these consultations to discuss how your theme translates to the specific spaces of your venue. Florists will often ask to see photos of your attire and venue to ensure the arrangements are proportional and the colours are complementary. If you are still looking for the right team to execute your vision, you can [find wedding vendors on Roko](/wedding-vendors) to compare styles and availability.

## Finalising the guest experience and ceremony details

Between three and six months before your wedding, the focus shifts from booking suppliers to defining the specific experience your guests will have. This is the period to send your official invitations, whether you choose traditional physical stationery or digital versions. Since many couples include menu options with their invites, you should confirm your wedding breakfast selection with your caterer before they are posted.

Catering is one of the most significant investments in the guest experience. Bridebook's 2026 UK Wedding Report found that the average spend on reception catering is £5,406, with evening food adding a further £2,002. These figures are closely tied to your guest count, with the average cost per guest across the UK sitting at approximately £278. As RSVPs begin to arrive, you can start the process of organising seating arrangements for the reception.

### Designing the ceremony
While the reception takes much of the planning energy, the ceremony requires specific decisions during this window:

*   Select your readings and decide who will perform them.
*   Choose the music for your walk down the aisle.
*   Finalise the timings for the service with your officiant or celebrant.

If you are still looking for specialists to manage your guest experience, you can [find wedding vendors on Roko](/wedding-vendors) to help manage everything from bespoke catering to ceremony music.

### Catering budget benchmarks

| Category | Average spend (as of 2026) |
| :--- | :--- |
| Reception catering | £5,406 |
| Evening catering | £2,002 |
| Wedding cake | £360 |

Finalising these details now ensures that the logistics are settled before you enter the final two months of preparation, when the focus moves to final fittings and speeches.

## The final countdown: fittings and speeches

As you enter the final one to three months, the focus shifts from booking to refining. This is the period to contact every supplier to confirm that arrangements match your expectations.

### Final fittings and attire
Schedule your final dress or suit fittings during this window. These appointments ensure the fit is perfect and allow you to practise moving, sitting and walking in your wedding attire. It is also the time to ensure all accessories, from shoes to jewellery, are ready.

### Creating the wedding timeline
A detailed, minute by minute schedule is essential for a smooth flow. Your timeline should account for:

*   Arrival times for the wedding party and hair and makeup artists.
*   The start of the ceremony and any travel between locations.
*   The wedding breakfast and specific milestones like the cake cutting and first dance.

If your venue has an on the day coordinator, they will use this document to manage the event. You can find experienced professionals to help manage these logistics by browsing [wedding vendors](/wedding-vendors) on Roko.

### Writing and ordering the speeches
Decide on the order of the wedding speeches and begin writing them now. While some people plan to write their words the night before, Roko recommends finishing drafts at least a month in advance. This allows time to:

*   Rehearse delivery out loud to check the rhythm and timing.
*   Build confidence, especially if you are nervous about public speaking.
*   Ensure the tone strikes the right balance for your audience.

Having your speech ready early removes a significant source of stress in the final weeks, leaving you to focus on the celebration itself.

## The week of the wedding: logistics and payments

The final seven days shift focus from creative decisions to practical execution. Most of your energy should go towards ensuring that the professionals you have hired can perform their roles without needing to interrupt you for directions.

### Final supplier logistics
Contact every business on your list to confirm exact arrival times. Once these are set, share the schedule with your venue. If your venue provides an on the day coordinator, this is the moment to hand over the reins. Provide them with a master list of supplier phone numbers and their scheduled arrival windows so they can manage any delays or questions on your behalf.

### Settling outstanding balances
Aim to have all supplier payments finalised before the week begins. Settling these accounts early ensures you are not managing bank transfers or chasing invoices during the celebration. If you are still looking for specific specialists for these final touches, the [Roko Directory](/wedding-vendors) lists professionals across all categories who can assist with last minute requirements.

### The wedding emergency kit
Pack a small bag of essentials to keep with you or your wedding party. According to Bridebook, this kit should include:

* Plasters for blisters or new shoes
* Painkillers
* Safety pins for unexpected wardrobe issues

### Rehearsals and trial runs
If you feel nervous about the ceremony, a final rehearsal at the venue is a practical way to settle those feelings. Use this time to walk through the order of service with your wedding party. Many couples choose to follow this with a dinner, which provides a relaxed opportunity for the wedding party and immediate family to meet before the main event begins.

## Regional variations and destination considerations

Where you choose to marry has a significant impact on your total spend. According to Bridebook's 2026 UK Wedding Report, while the national average wedding cost is £20,604, regional prices vary by thousands of pounds. 

### How location affects your budget

London remains the most expensive region in the UK, with an average total cost of £26,986. This is largely because supplier costs in the capital typically run 30 percent above the national average. Conversely, couples marrying in Yorkshire and the Humber often find supplier costs are around 12 percent below the UK average. 

| Region | Average Cost (2026) |
| :--- | :--- |
| London | £26,986 |
| Scotland | £22,987 |
| South East England | £22,637 |
| North West England | £17,342 |

If you are looking for specific specialists in these areas, you can browse [all event and wedding businesses](/wedding-vendors) on the Roko Directory to compare styles and service levels. 

### Planning a wedding abroad

For those taking their celebration overseas, such as to Mallorca, the checklist requires additional logistical steps. Practicality should dictate what travels with you and what you source on site.

*   **Attire and valuables:** Always carry your wedding dress or tailored suit in the aircraft cabin rather than checking it into the hold. Keep rings, jewellery and essential legal documents in your personal hand luggage.
*   **Local sourcing:** Items like furniture, large décor and flowers are almost always better sourced locally to avoid high freight costs and customs complications.
*   **Supplier travel:** If you plan to bring a UK-based photographer or hair stylist, you must account for their travel, accommodation and potential work permit requirements. Post-Brexit rules mean customs treatment for professional equipment can be complex, so confirm these details before booking.

When planning from a distance, hiring a local coordinator can help manage these regional specifics and ensure your day meets the high standards you expect.
